findings.message: The elements draw 48.0 A hot at 240 V. At +5 % supply voltage (ANSI C84.1 Range A) that is 50.4 A, and 52.7 A while the wire is cold, against the 48 A continuous limit. Kiln makers rate kilns the same way.

The tool chose 6 elements of 9 AWG wire (2.91 mm): the fewest elements that work, each with the thickest wire whose coil fits its groove. Kanthal recommends wire of 3 mm or more for the longest life in grooves. No number of elements in the left, right, back and front walls fits wire that thick, because its coils would be longer than the grooves. Expect to replace these elements sooner.
Electrical work must follow your local code and be checked by a licensed electrician. These results are engineering guidance, not an approved design.

A round electric kiln's bricks are held by steel bands, not mortar: 3 round the wall, one round each 9 in section; one round the floor slab; one round the lid. Their width, thickness and tension aren't sized: no source found gives them, so take them from the maker of the bands or a kiln of the same size.
findings.reference: electric-kiln-survey.md: L&L e23T-3, 9 in sections; Skutt's lid, slab and body bands, the bricks held by the band's tension, not cement (kiln parts listings, snippets)

findings.message: The kiln loads from the top: the lid is the flat roof's slab of mortared straights in a steel band, and the band carries the lid's hinge on one side and a handle opposite it to lift it by. The walls have no door. UL 499 holds a handle grasped to lift to 55 °C if metal, 75 °C if not. The hinge and handle aren't sized: no source found gives their size or steel, so take them from the maker of the bands or a kiln of the same size.
findings.reference: electric-kiln-survey.md (the lid's band carries the hinge, the user); electric-kiln-hardware.md §1.1 [S8] [S1] (bands round the lid and floor slab), §7.1 [S16] (a lid lifter), §8.4 (UL 499, Table 36.2: handles)

findings.message: 3 peepholes, 1 in round, through the wall, as the kiln has no door: each in the middle of a 9 in section, between its two courses' element grooves, as L&L drills a two-row section square to the case (more holes than sections are spaced evenly). No maker gives their heights.

Round kiln: Round wall, layer 1 from the inside: 3 in ring of 6 courses of 12 straight cut to the angle, each cut at both ends 15.0° off square, its 9 in outside face whole; Floor, layer 1 from the inside: a 12-sided slab of mortared straights, 34.8 in across its corners, 19 whole and 12 cut to the kiln's profile, a steel band round it, not hinged; Roof, layer 1 from the inside: a 12-sided slab of mortared straights, 34.8 in across its corners, 19 whole and 12 cut to the kiln's profile, a steel band round it carrying the lid's hinge. Tapered rings follow Olsen's circle tables. A 4½ in ring is the builder's choice (the design's chamber.rings): straights with mortar-filled wedge joints, as Olsen draws a curved wall (Fig. 2-13, p.45); straights cut to the angle, the norm in electric kilns; straights with featheredges; or arch bricks, possible but not recommended (p.45). This one: cut. Cut rings are stacked course on course, their facets in line: in small kilns, electric especially, a smooth wall matters more than staggered joints (the user, a kiln builder). Brick counts assume dry joints at the nominal size, but for the wedge joints said; the breakage allowances are those of a box kiln (allowance.py).
findings.reference: Olsen, The Kiln Book, 4th ed., p.21, p.45, p.303–305 (kiln-reference.md, Brick sizes and shapes; Walls, bonds and openings; Tables A-4 to A-7); Olsen, The Kiln Book, 4th ed., p.45, Fig. 2-13: straights on the curve, their joints opening toward the outside; HarbisonWalker featheredge, 9 × 4½ × (2½ − ⅛) in (kiln-hardware.md §5.1 [S20]); straights with featheredges, and straights cut to the angle, the norm in electric kilns (the user, a kiln builder, 2026-10-30); 9 × 4½ × 2½ in straight; electric-and-thermal.md §5 [S54]
